role.altitude: The philosophy lecturer keeps reading, arguing, deciding curriculum changes, chairing the department and talking with students; answering routine mail, typing minutes, collecting evaluation results, building teaching rosters in spreadsheets and arranging appointments by mail shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking literature summaries against the sources
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer who spends more of the week on texts, arguments and students.

tasks.short: Handle department mail, chair meetings, prepare agendas and minutes, plan teaching assignments, approve budgets, and handle staff and student issues to perform administrative duties such as department head.

steps.what: Department head handles department mail and routine requests
Department head chairs department meetings
Department head prepares the agenda and writes the minutes

loop.input: The agenda and the head's notes of decisions and actions.
loop.output: Draft minutes with decisions and actions per agenda item.
loop.check: The head reads the whole draft against their own notes: every decision and action must match what was decided, with the owner and date from the notes; anything not in the notes is removed, and unclear points are written by hand.
loop.stop: The head approves the minutes, or writes them by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Notes are shorthand and vary by meeting.

steps.what: Department head checks the final minutes before they go to staff: decisions, actions, owners and dates as agreed in the meeting
Department head sends the checked minutes to the department staff
Department head plans teaching assignments for staff
Department head looks up spend against budget for each budget request and expense: across reports today, in one view after the change
Department head decides each budget item and expense: amount, purpose and budget line against what is left
Department head approves the decided items in the finance system
Department head handles staff and student issues

tasks.design: Standard replies for routine requests about courses, rooms and procedures shorten mail handling a little. Chairing and handling people's issues stay with the head. A drafting step turns the agenda and the head's notes into minutes with an owner and date per action; the head reads the draft against the notes, corrects it, checks the final version and sends it. Teaching assignments are planned in a workload model with contract hours and course hours per person, which shows over- and under-loading, instead of a spreadsheet rebuilt each year. Budget approvals use a view of spend against budget instead of several reports; the head still decides each item and approves it once in the finance system. Assignments follow hours and expertise only.

approvals.approved_version: The minutes with each decision, action, owner and date exactly as checked by the head in s3b, sent once to the department staff list for this meeting; any change needs a new check.
Each budget item and expense with amount, purpose and budget line exactly as decided by the head in s5b, approved once in the finance system for payment; any change needs a new decision.

tasks.previous_blocker: Minutes, rosters and budget checks were done by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Workload models, budget views and drafting from notes.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a small department working together.

evidence.claim: Minutes can be drafted from notes and checked by the chair.
Systems able to monitor staff need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: department administration; serving on committees (task 6391) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s4: course hours from the timetable and contract hours from HR.

Chairing and people issues keep their full time. Minutes keep 70 because the head still reads and corrects every draft; deciding and approving budget items keep their full time, only the look-up in s5 is shorter.
research_questions: Are minutes out sooner and actions closed more often?

incremental.description: Department head keeps the workload model and standard replies current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the head rewrites most drafted minutes and contract hours are not linked from HR, so s3 keeps 85 and s4 keeps 80 (10.2); high: drafts and the workload model used as designed (15.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find and screen literature for the project, read and analyse texts and develop the argument, write the article or book, and submit and handle peer review to conduct research and publish findings.

steps.what: Lecturer finds and screens literature for the research project

loop.input: The research question and the library's databases.
loop.output: Topic summaries and a list of foundational and recent works.
loop.check: Every reference must resolve in the catalogue or by DOI, and the lecturer screens each listed item by its abstract against the research question; topic summaries orient only and are never cited.
loop.stop: The lecturer ends the search when no new relevant works appear.
loop.why_not_simpler: Philosophical topics use varied terms across traditions.

steps.what: Lecturer reads and analyses texts and develops the argument
Lecturer writes and formats the article or book manuscript
Lecturer checks the final manuscript before submission: each citation supports the claim it is attached to, the bibliography matches the text, and the journal's requirements are met
Lecturer submits the checked manuscript to the journal or publisher
Lecturer responds to peer review and revises until the findings are published

tasks.design: A literature tool gives topic summaries and lists foundational papers, and every reference is checked against the catalogue before the lecturer reads it, so the first search takes less time. Reading, analysis and the argument stay fully with the lecturer. A reference manager formats citations and the bibliography and the publisher's template sets the layout, so formatting takes less time; writing the manuscript stays with the lecturer. Submission and peer review stay as they are.

approvals.approved_version: The manuscript with text, citations and bibliography exactly as checked by the lecturer in s4b, submitted once to the journal or publisher named in it; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Literature searches went database by database.
tasks.enabler_now: Literature tools with topic summaries and catalogue checks.
tasks.still_hard: Older and non-English works poorly covered by databases.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the objection no one has answered.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; thinking and writing stay.

evidence.claim: A literature database tool gives topic summaries and foundational papers.

assumptions: Boundary: research and publishing; writing articles and books (task 20105) and keeping up with literature (task 6383) are sibling tasks.

Priced here: the answer for sibling task 20105 does not cut the manuscript. s3 keeps 85: a reference manager formats citations and the bibliography and the publisher's template sets the layout; the writing itself keeps its full time.
Analysis and peer review keep their full time.
unknowns: How much of the search is in poorly indexed sources.
research_questions: Does the first literature round take less time without missing key works?

incremental.description: Lecturer drops references that do not resolve.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: work on older texts that the databases cover poorly, so finding literature keeps 90 (5.5); high: recent debates well covered, as designed (8.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather course evaluations and grade results, evaluate and plan revisions to curricula and methods of instruction, map outcomes to assessments, revise course content and materials, and submit changes to the programme committee.

steps.what: Lecturer gathers course evaluation results and grade distributions
Lecturer evaluates the course and plans revisions to curricula and methods of instruction
Lecturer maps learning outcomes to assignments and exams
Lecturer revises course content and materials
Lecturer fills the change form for the programme committee: from scratch today, with catalogue fields pre-filled after the change
Lecturer checks the final change form: the pre-filled catalogue fields match the revised course and the rationale states the changes made
Lecturer submits the checked course changes to the programme committee

tasks.design: A course dashboard in the learning platform shows evaluation scores, comments and grade distributions per assessment, instead of exporting and combining them by hand. Evaluating and planning revisions stay with the lecturer. Learning outcomes are linked to assignments in the platform, so the outcome map updates when an assessment changes. The change form for the programme committee is pre-filled from the course catalogue; the lecturer writes the rationale, checks the form and submits it once. Revising materials belongs to the course materials task and is priced there.

approvals.approved_version: The change form with the revised course's catalogue fields and rationale exactly as checked by the lecturer in s5b, submitted once to the programme committee's queue for this course; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Results were exported and combined by hand and the outcome map lived in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Course dashboards and outcome mapping in learning platforms.
tasks.still_hard: Low response rates on course evaluations.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which classic text to drop for a new debate.

ambition.what: Adjust the course after each run instead of every few years.

reach.learn: Whether proposals come with clearer evidence.

evidence.claim: An assessment platform provides item statistics per question.

assumptions: Boundary: evaluating and revising curricula; preparing course materials (task 6381) and collaborating with colleagues (task 6392) are sibling tasks.
s4 is part of preparing course materials, which sibling task 6381 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s1: evaluations and grades in the learning platform.
Evaluating and planning keep their full time.
s5 keeps 70 because the rationale for the changes is still written by the lecturer; only the catalogue fields are pre-filled. The check and submission (s5b, s5c) keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether course evaluations sit in the same platform.
research_questions: Do revisions follow evaluation results more closely?

incremental.description: Lecturer links outcomes to new assignments.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: part of the evaluations are collected outside the platform, so gathering results keeps 70 (14.1); high: all results in the course dashboard (20.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Let students book office hours, arrange appointments, advise and assist students in office hours, and follow up with resources.

steps.what: Student books an office-hours slot
Lecturer arranges office-hours appointments with students
Lecturer advises and assists students during office hours
Lecturer follows up by mail with readings or resources

tasks.design: Students book office-hours slots on a booking page linked to the lecturer's calendar, instead of mailing to find a time. Advising and follow-up stay personal.
tasks.still_hard: Students who need help but do not book.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a question about an essay is really about something else.

reach.learn: Whether students find a slot sooner.

evidence.claim: Booking pages linked to calendars replace arranging by mail.

assumptions: Boundary: office hours; advising on curricula and careers (task 6388) is a sibling task.
Students' booking time is shown in s1 at share 1, about what a mail took.
Advising and follow-up keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of students who book online.
research_questions: Do more students use office hours?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of students still mail to find a time, so arranging keeps 65 (5.1); high: most appointments booked on the page (10.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
